history_note: T0030 through T0035 are PRESERVED unchanged. Migration 0014 is preserved; 0015 corrects it additively.

corrections.what_was_actually_true: 0014 enforced 'one live CHARGE per settlement' and the cumulative refund bound with SELECT-then-decide logic inside a BEFORE INSERT trigger. Two concurrent transactions each read the pre-state, each pass, and both commit. A count() in a trigger is not a constraint, and the sequential tests covering it could not tell the difference between a constraint and a lucky ordering.
corrections.correction: The duplicate-charge bound is now the partial unique index ptx_one_live_charge_per_settlement -- not a check but an impossibility. The cumulative refund bound takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock on the PARENT (namespace 47) before summing, so children of one parent serialize and different parents never contend.
corrections.proved: iam_v2_scratch/phase4_payment_concurrency.sh, 7 PASS / 0 FAIL, with REAL concurrent psql sessions: two differently-keyed CHARGEs racing leave exactly one live charge and the loser names the unique index; two individually-valid 60-unit refunds against a captured 100 do not both commit and the loser names the cumulative bound while the winner is still uncommitted; an unrelated settlement is unaffected and does not wait.

corrections.what_was_actually_true: 0014 also permitted REQUIRED -> FAILED and REQUIRED -> MANUAL_REVIEW directly, letting a settlement reach a terminal state without ever having been attempted. Contract section 16 is REQUIRED -> IN_PROGRESS -> SETTLED | FAILED | MANUAL_REVIEW.
corrections.correction: REQUIRED now transitions only to IN_PROGRESS, and apply_payment_callback_v2 establishes IN_PROGRESS and the terminal state in the same transaction.

corrections.what_was_actually_true: p_detail was arbitrary jsonb persisted verbatim into an append-only financial ledger, guarded only by a comment asking callers not to send payloads.
corrections.correction: p4_callback_evidence_safe enforces a closed flat key set, 200-character values, no nesting or arrays, no control characters, and heuristic screening for credentials, key literals and card-like digit runs. It is a CHECK constraint on the table as well as a function-argument check, so it holds for every writer. Provider event ids and types are bounded too. The guarantee is stated as structurally closed and heuristically screened -- not as a proof.

corrections.what_was_actually_true: apply_payment_callback took the INTERNAL transaction id as an argument, so the caller decided which money the provider was talking about. Dedupe keyed on (payment_transaction_id, provider_event_id) let one provider event be applied to two different internal rows simply by naming a different one.
corrections.correction: apply_payment_callback_v2 resolves the transaction from the provider's own identity -- tenant + provider + merchant account + the client reference the provider echoed back -- and has no argument in which a caller could name a transaction. Dedupe is now UNIQUE (tenant, provider, merchant_account, provider_event_id). An uncorrelated callback raises CALLBACK_UNCORRELATED and is not applied. The 0014 entry point is DROPPED so exactly one callback door exists.

corrections.what_was_actually_true: Child payment state and Settlement state were independently writable, so the authoritative status could disagree with its own arithmetic.
corrections.correction: A captured REFUND or CHARGEBACK moves the Settlement to PARTIALLY_REVERSED or REVERSED in the SAME transaction, computed from the durable child sums.

corrections.what_was_actually_true: mg7 made provider_ref NOT NULL and 0014 made it immutable, so no row could exist before the provider had answered. That is precisely the crash window in which a provider takes money and StayConnect has no durable record of having intended it.
corrections.correction: provider_ref is now explicitly the LOCAL durable intent reference, generated before any external call and unique per tenant/provider/merchant -- an idempotency root that survives a crash. provider_txn_ref is a new nullable, write-once column for the reference the provider assigns, with its own partial unique index. A transaction must be created as CREATED and may not carry a provider reference at creation.
corrections.provider_contract_assumption: This design requires a provider that accepts a client-supplied reference on the charge request and ECHOES IT BACK on every callback about that charge. That is common (Stripe client_reference_id/metadata, Adyen merchantReference, Checkout.com reference) but NOT universal, and no provider integration in this milestone has been verified against a real endpoint. A provider without that capability would need a different correlation strategy, and adopting one is a separate, evidenced decision.

not_delivered_in_this_milestone: The Go payment DOMAIN and deterministic provider doubles are NOT implemented. 0015 completes the durable contract the runtime will sit on; no Go service creates charges, calls a provider double, or applies callbacks through it.

The Phase-2 atomic Entitlement grant is NOT wired to payment success. No second entitlement writer was created; the existing controlled path in internal/iamv2/commerce_flow.go remains the one to reuse.
The Phase-4 least-privilege DB grant model is NOT designed or applied.
Frontend, FINANCIAL_RECOVERY_MODE, observability, runtime PMS ownership integration, live-DARK deployment and reboot/rollback all remain outstanding.
